title: Normalized evaluation on an etale object with a torsor section
statement: With the fixed connected torsor c:Y -> V, coefficient prime ell, sheaf F, constant value A, pullback trivialization, and normalized alpha:F -> Q_F as in [def-weil-pbc-torsor-section-representation], [def-weil-connected-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], let W be an etale V-object and suppose a morphism f:W -> Y over V is supplied. Then alpha_W is bijective. The extra morphism makes the torsor above W split; no assertion is made here for objects without such a morphism.

source.place: Tags 0DV5 (3), 0DV6 and 0A3R, proof identifying the restricted representation; sites.tex Tags 04TR and 04TS (gluing sheaves and mapping property), with module operations as in 0DV5 (3); explicit section-evaluation implementation of the fixed-torsor argument

proof.text: Apply the proved graphEvaluation_injective lemma to the canonical representation on F(Y). Graph values determine the equivariant function on every translate. No extension construction or surjectivity of graph evaluation is needed.

Forget the equivariance proof of alpha componentwise to construct the ordinary linear evaluation beta. Naturality of alpha implies the pointwise restriction equation for beta, and the supplied diagonal normalization is exactly beta normalization. Apply ordinaryGraphEvaluation_bijective to get bijectivity of graph evaluation composed with alpha.

The composite is injective, so alpha is injective. For any equivariant section q, composite surjectivity supplies s with the same graph values as q; graph injectivity gives alpha(s)=q. This is Function.Bijective.of_comp_left in Lean.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0DV5 (3), 0DV6 and 0A3R, proof identifying the restricted representation; sites.tex Tags 04TR and 04TS (gluing sheaves and mapping property), with module operations as in 0DV5 (3); explicit section-evaluation implementation of the fixed-torsor argument; explicit graph evaluation and constant-coordinate steps of the local fixed-torsor argument
proof_origin.note: H2 reduction: graph injectivity is proved by the existing base-change splitting lemma; ordinary normalized graph coordinates are isolated. Alpha is proved bijective by cancellation of the injective graph map. No equivariant extension is needed.

mathlib_searches.query: Normalized evaluation of sections of a constant sheaf on a connected Galois cover is bijective on objects with a section of the cover
A constant sheaf on a connected scheme has global sections equal to its coefficient module and sections on etale objects are locally constant functions
mathlib_searches.results: StructureSheaf.toOpen_eq_const, ModuleCat.Tilde.res_const and exists_const, Scheme.Γ_obj_op: no applicable etale torsor evaluation theorem. Related project constant-sheaf global sections and localization restriction inspected.
Only the parent, evaluation existence, representation definitions and downstream essential-image caller. No independent local bijectivity declaration in either library root or Mathlib.

lean.statement:
theorem Scheme.GaloisCover.sectionEvaluation_bijective_of_section
    {V : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace V] (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (P : Type u) [Group P] [Finite P]
    (c : Scheme.GaloisCover (ULift.{u + 1} P) V) [ConnectedSpace c.P]
    (F : Sheaf V.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ))))
    (A : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)))
    (h : Nonempty ((c.π)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ))].obj F ≅
      (constantSheaf c.P.smallEtaleTopology
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)))).obj A))
    (α : F.obj ⟶ c.sectionRepresentationPresheaf ℓ F)
    (hα : c.SectionEvaluationNormalized ℓ F α) (W : V.Etaleᵒᵖ)
    (f : W.unop ⟶ c.sectionObject) :
    Function.Bijective (α.app W)
